Probe, polarization and assembly

In the longitudinal section, A is measured inside the can from the closed back to the axis of the probe. The probe extends inward by P, including the connector pin. The open end radiates primarily along the can axis.
Aperture view. A horizontal line spans the diameter D. The probe and the main electric field at the center are vertical.
The aperture view shows the direction of the dominant TE₁₁ electric field near the center. It follows the probe. Rotating the can around its axis by 90° switches vertical and horizontal polarization.
Elepal’s flare example uses a 100 mm throat and 170 mm opening, a 132 mm can, a 44 mm probe offset and a 31 mm probe. The arrow shows the main beam direction.

3G-Aerial estimates 4–6 dBi for the basic can. Elepal reports an improvement of about 3 dB from a flare in its example. These figures describe different builds. Gain and beamwidth depend on the aperture, feed and measurement conditions.
1. Use a smooth metal cylinder with a conductive back. Measure the inside diameter. Start with L ≈ 3λg/4. If you trim the can, leave enough metal to finish the edge.
2. Mark the connector axis at A ≈ λg/4. Drill to fit the actual connector. Remove paint at the contact and make sure the connector shell bonds to the can. Start with a probe projection P ≈ λ₀/4.

3. Use short low-loss coax. Match the receiving antenna’s polarization, aim using a signal-level indicator and adjust the probe in small steps. For outdoor use, add a suitable RF-transparent cover and a drain at the lowest point.
